questions.question_text:
Two rectangular prisms have the same volume. Prism A has dimensions $x\text{ cm}$, $3\text{ cm}$ and $2\text{ cm}$. Prism B has dimensions $7.5\text{ cm}$, $4\text{ cm}$ and $5\text{ cm}$.

options.why: Found Prism B's volume correctly, then divided by $3$ only, ignoring Prism A's other known dimension of $2\text{ cm}$.
Found Prism B's volume correctly, then divided by $2$ only, ignoring Prism A's other known dimension of $3\text{ cm}$.
Used $7.5 \times 4 = 30$ as Prism B's volume, omitting its third dimension, then divided by Prism A's cross-sectional area of $6\text{ cm}^{2}$.

questions.solution_text:
Prism B: $V = (7.5 \times 4) \times 5$
$= 150\text{ cm}^{3}$
Prism A: $A = 3 \times 2$
$= 6\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$150 = 6x$
$x = 25\text{ cm}$
